fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The name Ba’al is feared by Abrahamic religious types, and that aversion has concealed a linguistic key that connects systems of power, priesthood, and rulership across time and history, worldwide.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In this episode of Inner Whirled, we trace the name Ba'al through languages, mythologies, and historical systems, revealing how a single root appears everywhere: Baal, Bel, Bol, Vul, El, Allah, Adonai, Jupiter, Adonis. From ancient temples and pyramidal structures to the gilded cage of modern feudalism, we demonstrate how Ba'al reveals the blackest form of magic practiced by the ruling classes of all ages, not an obscure Old Testament character but a universal pattern of authority embedded in language, religion, and society itself. In Part 2 we move from symbolism into structure. Ba'al begins to appear not just as a god, but as Dharma, justice, and law itself, embodied in the bull that upholds cosmic order. How does that symbol translate into priesthoods, papal power, and the systems that claim authority over all humanity? From the Triple Crown of Ba'al to papal bulls and modern banking, we trace a continuous pattern where religion, law, and debt converge into one system. If currency is debt, and debt is ownership, are we participants in the system, or its property?

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Baal as the Dharma and the God of Justice", "body": "The exclusive hour opens by collapsing the distance between Buddhism and the Baal system. Edward Strachey is quoted saying Buddha, the son of Maia, is considered the god of justice, and the ox sacred to him is termed Dharma, an epithet confined to no individual or race. Godfrey Higgins reads the Bed of Dharma Raja at Mahabalipuram as a Bed of Melchizedek, since Raja and Malak both mean king while Dharma and sedek both mean justice. Hindu cosmology then depicts Dharma itself as a bull standing on four legs in the golden age and on one leg now."}, {"title": "The Triple Crown of Baal in Three Papal Bulls", "body": "Unam Sanctam, issued by Pope Boniface in 1302, is presented as the first express trust, declaring that every human creature must be subject to the Roman pontiff for salvation and effectively naming the Pope king of the world. Romanus Pontifex follows in 1455 under Nicholas V as the first testamentary trust, claiming all land as crown land in perpetuity. Aeterni Regis, issued by Sixtus IV in 1481 alongside the Treaty of Alcacovas, supplies the second crown and the birth certificate trust. A Council of Trent bull under Paul III completes the system known as feudal tenure."}, {"title": "Kings as Vassals and the Logic of Feudalism", "body": "The two swords doctrine holds that kings rule only by permission of the church, which makes a lord something other than a sovereign master. Lords receive their land from religious institutions and owe tithes upward, political authority is subordinate to the Pope, and the church may judge earthly rulers while the pontiff can be judged by no human authority except God. The conversation argues that this pyramid has a hidden level, with all European kings beneath the Pope in the temple at the missing capstone, and that the system arrived in Europe rather than originating there."}, {"title": "Property You Use But Never Own", "body": "If you can lose a house or car for failing to pay property tax, the argument goes, you are a user rather than an owner, and the next question is who holds the debt behind that arrangement. Older Rhode Island deeds converted sterling silver into land and described boundaries in meets and bounds with numbers spelled out in words. After 1933 made gold illegal and the public debt was made a trust, citizens became its perpetual collateral. Mortgages now run on Federal Reserve notes, which are themselves debt, and a debt cannot be satisfied with another debt."}, {"title": "Central Banking as the Real Spoil of War", "body": "A pattern is laid out across two centuries, from the first and second Banks of the United States and the War of 1812 through the Bank of France after the revolution, the Bank of Japan after the Boshin conflict, the Reichsbank after the Franco Prussian war, and central banks in Vietnam, Algeria and Bangladesh. Iraq and Afghanistan both acquired formally independent central banks after invasion, meaning banks reconnected to the IMF and World Bank. Iran, state owned and interest free since 1979 with no outstanding IMF loans, is read as the outstanding holdout in that sequence."}]
